executive_summary:
The host opens with updates on Brian Harpole's defamation suit against her. She says his lawyers have begun sending preservation orders, including an email asking her team for Ian Carroll's address. She also reports that Douglas Blake Bednarz – who, she and Baron Coleman (A-2545.1) note, has repeatedly and explicitly accused Harpole of detonating a charge that killed Charlie Kirk (A-2546) – was served with a preservation order by Dhillon Law Group rather than being sued. She recounts her own contacts with Bednarz, who offered unseen UVU footage he never delivered and in December turned to pressing her about Harpole. She says she stopped replying in mid-December, suspecting a trap.

The host revisits how military YouTubers tried to dissuade her from interviewing Mitch Snow. She reads messages in which one cited a Turning Point USA source saying TPUSA was giving her "rope to hang herself" while building a defamation suit (A-2548). She contrasts this with Harpole's filing, which says he ignored her three messages (A-2549.1) to avoid giving her an exclusive. She recalls Paramount Tactical accidentally airing Andrew Kolvet's Fort Huachuca alibi texts and shows a photo alibi she says carried the wrong dates (A-2550.1). She then reads her December 27 group text to Justin Streiff and Kolvet (A-2549.2) and her unanswered January 4 message to Dan Flood (A-2549.3).

In the second segment the host responds to a Jeremy Boreing video (A-2551.1) in which he says Daily Wire revenue grew every year he led it, and cites records alleging that her husband George Farmer was arrested in Nashville in August 2023 for DUI. Boreing says he learned of it while she still worked for him. The host denies that any incident or contact occurred during her tenure. According to the host, the Daily Wire found an incident report in late summer 2024 and pitched it to the New York Post, which declined. She argues that the aim of Boreing amplifying Laura Loomer's claims is to prompt a DHS inquiry into George's citizenship, which she says is baseless. She also says Pendragon, not her, damaged the company's finances.

The host raises the pending case against former Daily Wire camera operator Zachary Lewis, who is accused (not convicted) of child sexual abuse material offenses and who she says worked in the company's kids department. She also reads Boreing's X reply declining her invitation (A-2553), in which he says the arrest has nothing to do with him. In the comments she repeats that Blake Neff allegedly wrote Erika Kirk's speeches and that Aspen donors deny the CEO-appointment statement, and she says she received a new lead on Bednarz.

claims.label: Harpole's lawyers have begun sending preservation orders
claims.claim: The host says lawyers for Brian Harpole, in his defamation suit against her, have begun sending out preservation orders instructing recipients not to delete texts, Signal messages, emails or other communications.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the docket in Harpole v. Owens and any litigation-hold or preservation letters issued by plaintiff's counsel, with their recipients and dates.
claims.transcript_snippet: they are beginning to send out what are known as preservation orders, okay?

claims.label: Harpole's lawyers asked the host's team for Ian Carroll's address
claims.claim: The host says Harpole's lawyers emailed her team asking her to provide Ian Carroll's address, which she says she has never had.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the email from plaintiff's counsel to the host's team and any subsequent subpoena or preservation notice directed at Ian Carroll.
claims.transcript_snippet: their lawyers emailed my team wanting me to give them Ian Carroll's address.

claims.label: Ian Carroll guest-hosted during the host's maternity leave
claims.claim: The host says Ian Carroll was not a regular co-host or employee; he filled in while she was on maternity leave the previous year, and her show paid for his Airbnb.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the show's episode archive and production payment records for the period Ian Carroll guest-hosted.
claims.transcript_snippet: he just filled in for me while I was on maternity leave last year and we paid for his Airbnb while he did so.

claims.label: Military YouTubers claimed Mitch Snow never served or reached Fort Huachuca
claims.claim: The host says YouTubers including Paramount Tactical and Valhalla initially claimed that Mitch Snow had never been at Fort Huachuca, was a fraud and had never served in the military. She says both claims were later disproven.
claims.investigative_direction: Archive the Paramount Tactical / Valhalla streams and posts from that period, and compare them with Mitch Snow's military service records (DD-214) and Fort Huachuca base-access logs.
claims.transcript_snippet: First and foremost, that Mitch was never at Fort Huachuca, that he was a com- a complete fraud. He could not even get onto the base because he never even served in the military.

claims.label: Host says she verified Mitch Snow's videos' metadata and hotel receipts
claims.claim: The host says Mitch Snow recorded videos while at Fort Huachuca, that she examined their metadata, and that he submitted his hotel receipts to her.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original video files with their EXIF/metadata and the Fort Huachuca-area hotel folio for Mitch Snow's September 8–9, 2025 stay.
claims.transcript_snippet: He recorded videos while he was there because it was sort of a trip down memory lane from him from when he was serving. He also had submitted to me his hotel receipts.

claims.label: Ian Carroll relayed the military YouTubers' warnings to the host
claims.claim: The host says Ian Carroll, after failing to convince her, bowed out but delivered to her the warnings from the military YouTubers, who said they were in communication with lieutenant colonels.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Ian Carroll's messages to the host from that period and any communications between him and the Paramount Tactical / Valhalla hosts.
claims.transcript_snippet: Uh but of course did what they asked, delivered his warrant delivered their warnings, the military bro warnings.

claims.label: People who publicly accused Harpole of murder have not been sued
claims.claim: The host says some people online publicly and explicitly accused Brian Harpole of murdering Charlie Kirk, yet they have not been sued for defamation.
claims.investigative_direction: Search federal and state court dockets for defamation suits filed by Brian Harpole against anyone other than the host.
claims.transcript_snippet: And yet mysteriously I've been sort of watching and paying attention and those people are not being sued for defamation.

claims.label: Baron Coleman: Blake Bednarz accuses Harpole of murder daily
claims.claim: In a podcast clip played by the host, Baron Coleman says Blake Bednarz accuses Brian Harpole by name every day of murdering Charlie Kirk and has a video called "Judas Harpole."
claims.investigative_direction: Archive Blake Bednarz's X, YouTube and X Spaces output, including the "Judas Harpole" video, with dates.
claims.transcript_snippet: Blake Bednarz basically accuses by name Brian Harpole every single day of murdering Charlie Kirk. Like frame by frame. He has a whole video called Judas Harpole.

claims.label: Baron Coleman: Bednarz is not named in the Harpole lawsuit
claims.claim: Baron Coleman says Blake Bednarz is not listed in Harpole's lawsuit, even though Bednarz's content names Harpole.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the full Harpole complaint and its exhibits for any reference to Blake Bednarz or his posts, and check the list of named defendants.
claims.transcript_snippet: And yet, no, this Blake Bednarz's character is not listed in this lawsuit.

claims.label: Bednarz began his Harpole theories after the Shawn Ryan interview
claims.claim: The host identifies the person Coleman refers to as Douglas Blake Bednarz. She says he began positing theories about Harpole after Harpole's interview with Shawn Ryan, which she calls disastrous.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the publication date of Harpole's Shawn Ryan Show episode with the timestamps of Bednarz's first posts naming Harpole.
claims.transcript_snippet: The person he's referring to, a full name Douglas Blake Bednarz, and he certainly did not mince words when he began positing theories about Brian Harpole after Brian's disastrous interview with Shawn Ryan.

claims.label: Bednarz posted that Harpole triggered a detonation under Charlie Kirk's shirt
claims.claim: According to tweets read aloud by the host, Blake Bednarz posted that Brian Harpole wore controls under his clothes, triggered a shaped charge under Charlie Kirk's shirt, and that no gun was fired.
claims.investigative_direction: Archive the original Bednarz posts with URLs and timestamps, and compare the allegation with the autopsy and ballistics evidence in the Tyler Robinson case.
